question: Which divine guardians are assigned to protect the hair and the head?
premises: The wide-eyed one is invoked to protect the hair.
The beloved of the wind is invoked to protect the head.
Both protections are expressed as parallel requests.
inference: Different deities are assigned guardianship over specific parts of the body.
uncertainties: The exact identity of viśālākṣa in this context is not specified in the verse.
The identity of marutpriya is not explicitly named beyond the epithet.
plain_english: May the wide-eyed one protect the hair, and may the beloved of the wind protect the head.
